A.description: Identity coherence: exact equality of identity fields across canonical state, PDFs, JSON, MODEL, manifest.

B.description: Problem fidelity: the package answers the user's exact problem; invention is machine-linked to the objective.

C.description: Domain integrity: one canonical domain propagates through every layer; contradiction detector as second defense (primary invariant is field→source→domain).

F.description: Evidence integrity: one canonical ledger; count parity across machine layer, PDF class table, manifest; every item carries id/source/uri/hash/excerpt/class.

G.description: Causal mechanism integrity: the canonical chain PROBLEM→FAILURE→MECHANISM→INTERVENTION→EFFECT→BOUNDARY→DESIGN VARIABLES→FAILURE MODES→PREDICTION.

H.description: Engineering integrity: counts may not masquerade as maturity; DI/DO carry meaning/basis/status; ABSENT outputs may not be presented as existing.

I.description: Traceability: DI→parameter→DO→FM→VF→EXPERIMENT graph; broken links justified; critical-link gate.

J.description: Equations: every registry entry carries id/expression/variables/units/source/applicability; no slot-only rows.

K.description: Decisive experiment: falsification contract present — hypothesis/measurement/threshold etc. or explicit UNKNOWN; 'killer experiment fails: UNKNOWN' with nothing else is not acceptable.

L.description: Buyer decision quality: the first usable pages answer the buyer's next decision, not a completeness template.

M.description: Commercial integrity: every commercial number is SOURCE_FACT / ENGINEERING_ESTIMATE / ROUGH_ESTIMATE with assumptions, or NOT_ESTABLISHED (Art. LXVI).

N.description: 3D/artifact integrity: physical inventions must represent required components; software inventions are 3D_NOT_APPLICABLE; no generic substitute.

P.description: PDF visual QA: every PDF rendered and inspected — collision/overflow/clipping/blank-page/broken-symbol/missing-equation are hard failures.

Q.description: Manifest/ZIP integrity: actual files = manifest files = ZIP contents; SHA-256 per file; clean build — no stale/unmanifested artifacts.

R.description: State/maturity coherence: one canonical maturity with subordinate flags; no competing authorities.

T.description: Security: secret/credential/cookie/path scan must be clean before ZIP creation (values never printed).

U.description: Final independent semantic audit: does every major buyer-facing statement describe this exact technology?

V.description: Buyer language discipline (R440.6): raw JSON, exception strings, Python reprs, debug fields, route IDs and engine jargon never appear in buyer-facing PDFs.

W.description: Applicability integrity: buyer/manufacturing/regulatory/market requirements must match the problem's canonical context (the R443 domain-to-package semantic boundary; medical requirements in a non-medical problem are contamination, in a medical problem they are legitimate).
